title: 第三章 玉龙仙山第四章 玉龙秘境
content_zh:
;;
晨曦破开紫徽城笼罩的薄雾，金辉漫过巍峨的南门城楼时，四驾马车正踏着铁石长街，缓缓驶出城门。
马车皆以黑檀为架，嵌着细碎的银纹，四匹鬃毛油亮的高头大马奋蹄扬蹄，马蹄叩地，敲出整齐而沉稳的声响。车队周遭，二百名禁卫军身披玄甲，腰悬长刀，步履铿锵，将马车护于中央。队伍最前方，三骑战马呈品字排开，为首者面容刚毅，正是皇城禁军第三小队统领景涛将军，左右两侧各立一位副将，一人手中擎着墨色“秦”字大旗，一人高展赤色“景”字军旗，猎猎迎风作响。
景涛出身皇城四大家族之一的景氏，膝下第三子景曜，七岁那年测出上品土灵根，如今十岁，已练气三层，是碧霄仙宗外门第子。此番护送之行，便是因这层渊源，才由第三小队护送瑞安王，这为景氏家族后来成就星空家族起到关键的一环。
四驾马车的规制各有不同。头一辆马车车厢宽阔，帷幔低垂，内里端坐的正是碧霄仙宗的真君，他双目微闭，眉宇间蕴着淡淡的仙泽；紧随其后的第二辆马车，属于瑞安王与王妃，车厢外垂着水绿色的流苏，随着马车行进轻轻摇曳；第三辆马车内，四个年约十八的侍女，屏息凝神，皆是王府精挑细选的得力人手；最后一辆马车则堆满了箱笼，尽是些旅途所需的衣物、药材与日用之物。
待马车彻底驶出紫徽城的地界，前方引路的景涛将军抬手一挥，队伍的行进速度陡然加快。马蹄翻飞，卷起一路烟尘，朝着西北方向疾驰而去。
碧霄仙宗坐落于玉龙仙山之巅，与紫徽城相距千余里，其间山水迢迢，路途漫漫。车队一路行来，但凡途经炊烟袅袅的村落、商贾云集的小城，或是山明水秀的幽僻之地，都会停下休整片刻。真君也毫无仙长的架子，时常掀帘而出，与瑞安王这位秦家第二十七代的晚辈闲话家常，言语间亲和随意，倒让随行之人都松了几分拘谨。
这般走走停停，转眼便是十余日。视线尽头，原本平缓的地势渐渐起伏，化作连绵不绝的山脉，如巨龙蛰伏。官道渐窄，进入山林，车队循着蜿蜒的山道，一头扎进峡谷深处，再行三日有余，周遭已是人迹罕至，山林的凶兽咆哮声渐渐入耳，但在真君灵压下迅速退走。
当原有的车道也在此处断了踪迹时，眼前豁然开朗处，一方石砌围墙依山而建，墙内立着几间铁木搭建的院落，简陋却不失规整。院门口，一位身着青衫的筑基修士负手而立，面色沉静，身后跟着三名练气期的弟子，皆是碧霄仙宗派驻在此的接引之人。双方交接诸事妥当后，景涛将军朝着马车方向抱拳一揖，便领着两百禁卫军，循着来时路折返紫徽城。而真君、瑞安王与王妃一行人，则登上了筑基修士备好的飞行渡船。
这渡船乃是低阶灵器，通体由灵木与精铁锻造而成，论起防御、攻击之力，皆是平平无奇，飞行速度也称不上迅捷，胜在内部空间宽敞，即便容纳五十人也绰绰有余。渡船缓缓升空，冲破缭绕的云雾，众人皆移步至船甲之上，凭栏远眺。云雾在脚下流淌，如棉似絮，远处的山峦若隐若现，偶有灵鸟掠过天际，清啼声穿透云层传来，只觉心旷神怡。
这般御风而行，又是两日。起初，远处的玉龙仙山不过是一抹朦胧的黑影，待渡船愈发靠近，那黑影便一点点舒展身躯，化作一座巍峨耸峙的巨峰，直插云霄。峰峦叠翠间，隐约可见亭台楼阁错落有致，随着距离拉近，那些雕梁画栋的轮廓愈发清晰，飞檐翘角掩映在青松翠柏之间，随着云雾散去，渐渐露出了真切的模样。
渡船并未朝着山凹处直径十里的巨大广场飞去——那广场是碧霄仙宗弟子修行、比剑、迎客以及举办宗内庆典的之地，此刻正有不少身着各色服饰的弟子往来其间。渡船绕过广场，直朝着山腰最上方的一处别苑飞去，最终稳稳地停落在别苑外的一片茵茵草坪之上，别苑拱门上写着＂晨露苑＂几个苍劲大字。
瑞安王并非头一回来仙宗居住，这晨露苑，正是真君特意为他安排的。晨露苑的位置极佳，左侧二百丈开外，便是真君闭关清修的紫徽洞府，灵气最为浓郁；右侧偏低处五百丈开外，则是刑堂秦长老的洞府，隐隐透着几分威严之气。此地原是仙宗长老们闲暇时聚会议道、品茗弈棋的地方，自瑞安王一家入住后，长老们便默契地转去山腰的亭阁中交流，这处别苑，倒是渐渐成了瑞安王的专属居所。
送走真君后，瑞安王与王妃并肩而立，环顾着雅致清幽的院落，相视一笑。随即，二人唤来同行的四位侍从，吩咐他们洒扫亭台、整理屋舍，安置好随行的箱笼，又安排了膳食住宿。
暮色渐沉，远山如黛，晚风携着草木与灵气的清香，漫过院墙。一盏盏明灯被点亮，昏黄的光晕里，瑞安王夫妇坐在廊下，望着天边的弦月，只觉一路风尘俱寂，一段崭新而平静的仙山岁月，便这般悄然拉开了序幕。

The morning light broke through the mist shrouding Zihui City, and when the golden light spread over the towering south gate tower, four carriages were slowly driving out of the city gate along the long iron and stone street.
The carriages are all made of ebony, inlaid with fine silver patterns. Four tall horses with shiny manes are raising their hooves, and the horses' hooves are tapping the ground, making a neat and steady sound. Surrounding the motorcade, two hundred imperial guards were wearing black armor, with long swords hanging from their waists, and their steps were sonorous, guarding the carriage in the center. At the front of the team, three war horses were lined up in a row. The leader had a resolute face. He was General Jing Tao, the commander of the third squadron of the Imperial City Forbidden Army. There were two deputy generals on the left and right sides. One held an ink-colored flag with the word "Qin" in his hand, and the other held a red military flag with the word "Jing" high, hunting in the wind.
Jing Tao was born in the Jing family, one of the four major families in the imperial city, and the third son Jing Yao. When he was seven years old, he had a high-grade earth spirit root. Now he is ten years old and has reached the third level of Qi training. He is the son of the outer sect of the Bixiao Immortal Sect. It was because of this connection that the third team escorted King Ruian on this escort trip, which played a key role in the Jing family's later success in becoming the Starry Sky Family.
Regulations for four-horse carriages vary. The first carriage has a wide carriage with low curtains. The person sitting inside is the true king of the Bixiao Immortal Sect. His eyes are slightly closed, and there is a faint fairy light between his brows. The second carriage that follows closely behind belongs to King Ruian and the princess. There are aqua tassels hanging outside the carriage. As the carriage moved forward, it swayed gently; in the third carriage, four maids, about eighteen years old, were holding their breaths. They were all carefully selected capable men of the palace; the last carriage was filled with boxes and cages, filled with clothes, medicines and daily necessities needed for the journey.
When the carriage completely drove out of the boundaries of Zihui City, General Jing Tao, who was leading the way, raised his hand and the team's speed suddenly accelerated. The horse's hooves flew, picking up a trail of smoke and dust, and galloped towards the northwest.
The Bixiao Immortal Sect is located on the top of the Jade Dragon Immortal Mountain, more than a thousand miles away from Zihui City, with vast mountains and rivers and long roads. As the motorcade traveled along, it would stop for a moment whenever it passed through villages filled with smoke, small towns where merchants gathered, or remote places with beautiful mountains and rivers. Zhenjun also has no airs of immortality. He often lifts the curtain and comes out to chat with King Ruian, the twenty-seventh generation of the Qin family. His words are friendly and casual, which makes the people accompanying him relax a bit.
Stopping and going like this, it took more than ten days in the blink of an eye. At the end of the line of sight, the originally gentle terrain gradually undulated and turned into endless mountains, like a dormant dragon. The official road gradually narrowed and entered the mountain forest. The convoy followed the winding mountain road and plunged into the depths of the canyon. After more than three days of walking, the surrounding area was already deserted. The roars of the ferocious beasts in the mountain forest gradually became heard, but they quickly retreated under the spiritual pressure of the True Lord.
When the original driveway also disappeared here, a stone wall suddenly opened up in front of us. It was built against the mountain. Inside the wall stood several courtyards made of iron and wood. They were simple but neat. At the entrance of the courtyard, a foundation-building monk wearing a green shirt stood with his hands behind his hands, his face calm, followed by three disciples in the Qi training period, all of whom were stationed here to guide him from the Bixiao Immortal Sect. After the two sides handed over everything, General Jing Tao clasped his fists in the direction of the carriage and led the two hundred imperial guards back to Zihui City along the way they came. Zhenjun, King Ruian, and the princess boarded the flying ferry prepared by the foundation-building monks.
This ferry is a low-level spiritual weapon, made entirely of spiritual wood and fine iron. In terms of defense and attack power, it is mediocre, and its flight speed cannot be called fast. The advantage is that the interior space is spacious, and it is more than enough to accommodate fifty people. The ferry slowly lifted into the sky and broke through the lingering clouds and fog. Everyone moved to the ship's armor and leaned on the railing to look into the distance. The clouds and mist flowed under my feet, like cotton wool, and the mountains in the distance were looming. Occasionally, spiritual birds flew across the sky, and their clear cries came through the clouds. I felt relaxed and happy.
I walked like this against the wind for another two days. At first, the Jade Dragon Fairy Mountain in the distance was just a hazy black shadow., when the ferry got closer, the black shadow stretched out its body little by little, turning into a towering giant peak, reaching into the sky. Among the green peaks, pavilions and pavilions can be vaguely seen. As the distance gets closer, the outlines of those carved beams and painted buildings become clearer. The cornices are hidden among the green pines and cypresses. As the clouds and mists disperse, their true appearance is gradually revealed.
The ferry did not fly towards the huge square with a diameter of ten miles in the recess of the mountain - that square is the place where the disciples of the Bixiao Immortal Sect practice, compete with swords, welcome guests and hold sect celebrations. At this moment, there are many disciples wearing various costumes coming and going. The ferry flew around the square and flew straight towards a villa at the top of the mountainside. Finally, it landed steadily on a lawn outside the villa. On the arch of the villa were written "Chen Lu Yuan" in large and vigorous characters.
This was not the first time that King Ruian came to live in Xianzong. This Chenlu Garden was specially arranged for him by Zhenjun. The location of Chenlu Garden is excellent. Two hundred feet away on the left side is the Zihui Cave where Zhenjun retreats for meditation. It has the richest spiritual energy. Five hundred feet away on the lower right side is the cave of Elder Qin of the Punishment Hall, which has a faint aura of majesty. This place was originally a place where the elders of the Immortal Sect gathered for meetings, drank tea and played chess in their free time. After King Ruian's family moved in, the elders tacitly moved to the pavilion on the mountainside to communicate. This private garden gradually became King Ruian's exclusive residence.
After seeing off the true king, King Ruian and the princess stood side by side, looking around the elegant and quiet courtyard, smiling at each other. Immediately, the two summoned the four attendants who were accompanying them, and ordered them to clean the pavilion, tidy up the house, arrange the boxes and cages accompanying them, and arrange meals and accommodation.
The twilight is getting darker, the distant mountains are like black clouds, and the evening breeze carries the fragrance of vegetation and spiritual energy over the courtyard wall. The lamps were lit one after another, and in the dim light, Prince Ruian and his wife sat on the porch, looking at the crescent moon in the sky. They felt that the wind and dust were silent all the way, and a new and peaceful fairyland years had quietly begun.
